summary: The fix works for the reference-link cases I tried, but the PR also commits a leftover debugging file, tests/scratch_probe_issue7.py. It is unrelated to the change and deliberately fails when run.
verified: `python -m unittest discover tests` passes: 1170 tests, 52 skipped. The scratch file is not named test_*.py, so discovery never runs it.
A code-span label resolves for `[`a`][1]`, `[`a b`]` and `[`a`][]` against a matching definition. A label containing `<` and `&` also resolves.
The stray `[]` in `[a][1] [a b] [a][]` also appears with plain-text labels, so it is existing behaviour and not caused by this PR.
flake8 is clean on `markdown`, the changed test module and the scratch file.

findings.issue: A scratch probe script was committed to the repository. It is an unrelated file in the test tree. Its `test_probe` ends with `self.fail('probe')` and prints output for 26 inputs. `python -m unittest tests.scratch_probe_issue7` or an IDE test runner would run it and report a failure.
findings.evidence: diff.patch adds tests/scratch_probe_issue7.py (40 lines) with `self.fail('probe')`. The file exists at the PR head.

findings.issue: The new test names and docstrings use internal spec IDs (`test_ac_fr_001_1`, `AC-FR-001-1`). The repository's tests don't use that convention. The tests also don't cover mixed text and code in a label, or labels whose code contains special characters such as `&`, `<` or backticks. The new `code_span_source` function handles those cases.
